title: Beyond WASI: Running any Rust application in the browser with BrowserPod 3.0
excerpt: BrowserPod can now run real Rust programs in the browser, compiled from unmodified source with stock rustc and cargo.
content_html:
Today we are releasing BrowserPod 3.0, with full support for running any Rust application in the browser, many fixes for Node.js, and initial Python support.

Our Rust support goes beyond what can normally be achieved with the existing Wasm targets in terms of standard library features and third-party crate compatibility. Programs can access the filesystem, make network requests, run subprocesses, and interact with concurrently running applications. All of this without changing a single line of code!

In the demo below, you can see the preview version of Yarn 6 (written in Rust) installing an NPM project:

What is BrowserPod

BrowserPod is an in-browser code sandbox. Its goal is to make it possible to run any Linux application in modern browsers by compiling the application to WebAssembly and providing the full Linux syscall interface.

It provides an efficient, locally persistent virtual filesystem, outbound internet access for downloading packages or calling APIs, and inbound connections for exposing local development servers. BrowserPod supports real parallelism by running each thread or process on an independent Worker, while providing a consistent view of the system to all the running programs. For all purposes, it can be considered an OS kernel for the Web platform, implemented in WebAssembly.

This set of features makes BrowserPod uniquely suited for safe in-browser agentic code execution, web-based IDEs and development environments, interactive docs and live demos, educational platforms, and other applications that benefit from sandboxed execution inside a web app.

Why Rust now?

BrowserPod’s ambition is to run an entire Linux userspace in the browser. For the most part, this used to mean compiling a bunch of C/C++ projects. Most dynamic languages, such as Python, JavaScript or Ruby run on top of interpreters and runtimes that are also, most usually, written in C/C++, and so having a C/C++ toolchain (in our case, Cheerp) would get you very far.

Nowadays, this is less and less true. Popular languages like Rust and Go are compiled ahead of time like C/C++, and have their own toolchains.

Many build tools for Node.js in particular are being written (or rewritten) in Rust. For these reasons, Rust was always part of our roadmap for BrowserPod, but we decided to prioritize it over Python and Ruby thanks to a concrete use case from a member of our community on Discord.

One maintainer of the Yarn package manager expressed interested in building an interactive documentation page, featuring a real yarn build, and running on BrowserPod. But contrarily to previous versions, which were JavaScript, the upcoming Yarn 6 release is built in Rust.

This is one of the use cases where we think that BrowserPod can really shine, and so we started working on it right away! It took us a week to get to a first prototype and we could immediately see the potential, but there were more moving parts that we had expected.

What does it mean to “support” Rust

In previous releases of BrowserPod we focused on Node.js. Our users did not have to worry about compiling for the BrowserPod target, since we provide a pre-compiled Node.js build ourselves.

Rust programs behave very differently, since they need to be compiled ahead of time using rustc. As things stand today, the user needs to compile the program offline and add the resulting binary to the Pod. Interestingly, rustc itself is written in Rust. In principle, we could allow users to compile their Rust programs directly in the browser. We need a few additional features to achieve this objective, but it will happen in the near future.

Effectively “supporting Rust” today boils down to providing a Rust toolchain that can produce Wasm binaries for the BrowserPod target.

Existing Rust WebAssembly targets

Fortunately, we could start from solid ground. Rust already supports a variety of Wasm targets, namely:

  • wasm32-unknown-unknown: This target is the most barebones and platform agnostic. By itself, it makes no assumptions about the environment it runs in, but crates like wasm-bindgen and web-sys make it possible to communicate with the JS and Web environment. This target makes sense if you are deliberately targeting the Web from the start. Many standard library features are missing.
  • wasm32-unknown-emscripten: This target is intended for standalone programs targeting the Web. It can directly interact with JavaScript code, and already wraps many Web APIs for ease of use. It also emulates some POSIX APIs to an extent, but many Rust standard library features are not implemented. In general, supporting this target requires extensive rewriting.
  • wasm32-wasip1 / wasm32-wasip2 / wasm32-wasip3: These are the WASI targets. They can run in principle in any environment, although their main use is for WebAssembly outside of the browser. As such, they don’t assume the presence of JS, but they provide applications with I/O facilities like a filesystem and networking.
  • wasm32-wali-linux-musl: This target is intended to run existing Linux applications in a Wasm runtime, by providing the x86-64 Linux syscall interface as imports. Its main use case is outside of the browser, and it is currently mostly an academic project.

Why not just pick WASI?

Our original plan was to implement a WASI (WebAssembly System Interface) layer on top of BrowserPod. This solution would make any program targeting WASI immediately compatible with BrowserPod, whether it’s written in Rust, Go, C, or anything else.

But when trying to compile existing Rust programs to WASI, we quickly realized that it’s not just a matter of switching build targets.

Take yarn for example. Compiling it for WASI would require:

  • Platform-specific code to replace usage of std::os::unix with std::os::wasi: this is doable, although the mapping is not 1:1 (e.g. no absolute symlinks in WASI).
  • Removal of thread usage: wasm32-wasip3 has some limited cooperative threading support (without real parallelism), but it’s very new and supported by neither the standard library nor tokio.
  • Acceptance of reduced functionality: yarn relies on external programs for some functionality: in particular git (to fetch git dependencies) and node (to run lifecycle scripts) are required for basic operations.

BrowserPod already solves these problems, so we decided to skip the middleman and implement our own Rust target: wasm32-browserpod-linux-musl.

Making our own Rust target

Defining a custom Rust target is surprisingly easy: you define your target’s properties in a .json file:

And then pass the path of this file as the --target argument.

A few unstable features are needed, so we have to use a nightly version of the compiler. We also need to support our target in the Rust standard library for our combination of arch and os. Since it’s modeled after x86 Linux, we can mostly copy from that. And finally, we need to override a couple of foundational libraries: libc (we need to link to our own musl libc build) and linux-raw-sys (we just select the libc fallback).

A number of options to cargo and rustc are needed to tie everything together (unstable feature flags, the sysroot with the C dependencies, the cargo overrides for libc and linux-raw-sys, …); we provide wrapper scripts for them, so the user can compile with a simple cargo build --target wasm32-browserpod-linux-musl.

The hacks we did along the way

In an ideal world, this would be all we need. Unfortunately, we need to deal with the messy reality of third-party dependencies.

As mentioned, Rust already supports multiple Wasm targets. Many libraries can compile for one or more of those targets, but often with reduced functionality, or with the assumption that arch="wasm32" means “running in the browser’s main thread”, and other arbitrary constraints.

To reach our goal of compiling projects without changing the code, we need to dodge all the conditional compilation that would mistakenly categorize our target as a “reduced functionality” one.

If you look closer at the json snippet of our target definition above, you will notice two interesting things:

  • target_family: ["unix"]: originally, we had ["unix", "wasm"], but many crates use the wasm target family to mean “standalone web build”, “WASI”, “no filesystem”, or similar. Dropping “wasm” seems to be completely harmless.

  • arch: "wasm64": this is even more surprising, but unfortunately also necessary. arch="wasm32" is often used to detect standalone web targets (for example, reqwest will replace the whole HTTP client with a fetch() implementation). You would think that something would break because of this, but important info like the size of pointers is defined separately, and the actual target passed to the LLVM backend is still wasm32, so it all works out!

Of course, we would love to get rid of these hacks, but the proper solution requires awareness in the ecosystem that fully-featured Wasm targets exist, which will take time (but we have a plan).

The payoff

The original goal was to run yarn, but since our approach was completely general, we found that a lot of programs just work.

Or try it yourself at https://browsercode.io/agents/codex.

Using it

Rust has a single blessed package manager and build system: cargo. This makes it much easier for us to provide a good out-of-the-box developer experience compared to, say, C/C++.

Rust also has an official way to obtain and manage multiple toolchains: rustup. We can’t be distributed through rustup yet, because we are not an officially supported target, but we can install into its directories, so you can enable our toolchain for a single project in the usual way:

Future plans

I explained why the existing Wasm targets were not suitable for us, but I glossed over wasm32-wali-linux-musl.

Despite being aimed at native Wasm runtimes rather than browsers, WALI (WebAssembly Linux Interface) has the same core goal as BrowserPod: compile Linux applications unmodified to Wasm. The main difference really is that BrowserPod targets the x86 version of the Linux syscalls, while WALI targets the x86-64 version. The choice for BrowserPod comes from the fact that its syscall implementations are shared with CheerpX, which is a virtual machine for x86 Linux binaries (you may know it from WebVM).

CheerpX is working towards supporting x86-64 binaries, so in the future we could simply adopt WALI as our target (for both Rust and C/C++).

This would have many benefits:

  • it is already a supported Rust target
  • we could run the same Wasm binary both inside and outside of the browser
  • we could join forces in fixing the issues with third-party libraries upstream

We are very excited about this direction and will say more about it in the future!

Try it now

Head to console.browserpod.io to get an API key. You can find the documentation on browserpod.io/docs.

If you have a Rust project you’d like to see running in a browser tab (especially one you expect to break) we’d genuinely like to hear about it. Come find us on Discord.

blocks.html_en: In previous releases of BrowserPod we focused on Node.js. Our users did not have to worry about compiling for the BrowserPod target, since we provide a pre-compiled Node.js build ourselves.

sentences.en: In previous releases of BrowserPod we focused on Node.js.
sentences.zh: 在以前版本的 BrowserPod 中，我们专注于 Node.js。

sentences.en: Our users did not have to worry about compiling for the BrowserPod target, since we provide a pre-compiled Node.js build ourselves.

blocks.html_en: Rust programs behave very differently, since they need to be compiled ahead of time using rustc. As things stand today, the user needs to compile the program offline and add the resulting binary to the Pod. Interestingly, rustc itself is written in Rust. sentences.en: Rust programs behave very differently, since they need to be compiled ahead of time using rustc.
sentences.zh: Rust 程序的行为非常不同，因为它们需要使用 rustc 提前编译。

sentences.en: As things stand today, the user needs to compile the program offline and add the resulting binary to the Pod.
sentences.zh: 目前的情况是，用户需要离线编译程序并将生成的二进制文件添加到 Pod 中。

sentences.en: Interestingly, rustc itself is written in Rust.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，rustc 本身是用 Rust 编写的。

sentences.en: In principle, we could allow users to compile their Rust programs directly in the browser.
sentences.zh: 原则上，我们可以允许用户直接在浏览器中编译他们的 Rust 程序。

sentences.en: We need a few additional features to achieve this objective, but it will happen in the near future.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一些额外的功能来实现这一目标，但这将在不久的将来实现。

blocks.html_en: • wasm32-unknown-unknown: This target is the most barebones and platform agnostic. By itself, it makes no assumptions about the environment it runs in, but crates like wasm-bindgen and web-sys make it possible to communicate with the JS and Web environment. This target makes sense if you are deliberately targeting the Web from the start. Many standard library features are missing.

sentences.en: wasm32-unknown-unknown: This target is the most barebones and platform agnostic.
sentences.zh: wasm32-unknown-unknown：此目标是最准系统且与平台无关的。

sentences.en: By itself, it makes no assumptions about the environment it runs in, but crates like wasm-bindgen and web-sys make it possible to communicate with the JS and Web environment.
sentences.zh: 就其本身而言，它不会对其运行环境做出任何假设，但像 wasm-bindgen 和 web-sys 这样的包可以与 JS 和 Web 环境进行通信。

sentences.en: This target makes sense if you are deliberately targeting the Web from the start.
sentences.zh: 如果您从一开始就有意以 Web 为目标，则此目标是有意义的。

sentences.en: Many standard library features are missing.
sentences.zh: 缺少许多标准库功能。

blocks.html_en: • wasm32-unknown-emscripten: This target is intended for standalone programs targeting the Web. It can directly interact with JavaScript code, and already wraps many Web APIs for ease of use. It also emulates some POSIX APIs to an extent, but many Rust standard library features are not implemented. In general, supporting this target requires extensive rewriting.

sentences.en: wasm32-unknown-emscripten: This target is intended for standalone programs targeting the Web.
sentences.zh: wasm32-unknown-emscripten：此目标适用于针对 Web 的独立程序。

sentences.en: It can directly interact with JavaScript code, and already wraps many Web APIs for ease of use.
sentences.zh: 它可以直接与 JavaScript 代码交互，并且已经封装了许多 Web API 以方便使用。

sentences.en: It also emulates some POSIX APIs to an extent, but many Rust standard library features are not implemented.
sentences.zh: 它还在一定程度上模拟了一些 POSIX API，但许多 Rust 标准库功能并未实现。

sentences.en: In general, supporting this target requires extensive rewriting.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，支持这个目标需要大量的重写。

blocks.html_en: • wasm32-wasip1 / wasm32-wasip2 / wasm32-wasip3: These are the WASI targets. They can run in principle in any environment, although their main use is for WebAssembly outside of the browser. As such, they don’t assume the presence of JS, but they provide applications with I/O facilities like a filesystem and networking.

sentences.en: wasm32-wasip1 / wasm32-wasip2 / wasm32-wasip3: These are the WASI targets.
sentences.zh: wasm32-wasip1 / wasm32-wasip2 / wasm32-wasip3：这些是 WASI 目标。

sentences.en: They can run in principle in any environment, although their main use is for WebAssembly outside of the browser.
sentences.zh: 它们原则上可以在任何环境中运行，尽管它们的主要用途是在浏览器之外的 WebAssembly。

sentences.en: As such, they don’t assume the presence of JS, but they provide applications with I/O facilities like a filesystem and networking.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们不假设 JS 的存在，但它们为应用程序提供 I/O 设施，如文件系统和网络。

blocks.html_en: • wasm32-wali-linux-musl: This target is intended to run existing Linux applications in a Wasm runtime, by providing the x86-64 Linux syscall interface as imports. Its main use case is outside of the browser, and it is currently mostly an academic project.

sentences.en: wasm32-wali-linux-musl: This target is intended to run existing Linux applications in a Wasm runtime, by providing the x86-64 Linux syscall interface as imports.
sentences.zh: wasm32-wali-linux-musl：该目标旨在通过提供 x86-64 Linux 系统调用接口作为导入，在 Wasm 运行时中运行现有的 Linux 应用程序。

sentences.en: Its main use case is outside of the browser, and it is currently mostly an academic project.
sentences.zh: 它的主要用例是在浏览器之外，目前主要是一个学术项目。

blocks.html_en: Our original plan was to implement a WASI (WebAssembly System Interface) layer on top of BrowserPod. This solution would make any program targeting WASI immediately compatible with BrowserPod, whether it’s written in Rust, Go, C, or anything else.

sentences.en: Our original plan was to implement a WASI (WebAssembly System Interface) layer on top of BrowserPod.
sentences.zh: 我们最初的计划是在 BrowserPod 之上实现 WASI（WebAssembly 系统接口）层。

sentences.en: This solution would make any program targeting WASI immediately compatible with BrowserPod, whether it’s written in Rust, Go, C, or anything else.
sentences.zh: 该解决方案将使任何针对 WASI 的程序立即与 BrowserPod 兼容，无论它是用 Rust、Go、C 还是其他语言编写的。

blocks.html_en: But when trying to compile existing Rust programs to WASI, we quickly realized that it’s not just a matter of switching build targets.

sentences.zh: 但当尝试将现有 Rust 程序编译为 WASI 时，我们很快意识到这不仅仅是切换构建目标的问题。

blocks.html_en: • Platform-specific code to replace usage of std::os::unix with std::os::wasi: this is doable, although the mapping is not 1:1 (e.g. no absolute symlinks in WASI).

sentences.en: Platform-specific code to replace usage of std::os::unix with std::os::wasi: this is doable, although the mapping is not 1:1 (e.g. no absolute symlinks in WASI).
sentences.zh: 使用 std::os::wasi 替换 std::os::unix 的特定于平台的代码：这是可行的，尽管映射不是 1:1（例如 WASI 中没有绝对符号链接）。

blocks.html_en: • Removal of thread usage: wasm32-wasip3 has some limited cooperative threading support (without real parallelism), but it’s very new and supported by neither the standard library nor tokio.

sentences.en: Removal of thread usage: wasm32-wasip3 has some limited cooperative threading support (without real parallelism), but it’s very new and supported by neither the standard library nor tokio.
sentences.zh: 删除线程使用：wasm32-wasip3 有一些有限的协作线程支持（没有真正的并行性），但它非常新，并且标准库和 tokio 都不支持。

blocks.html_en: • Acceptance of reduced functionality: yarn relies on external programs for some functionality: in particular git (to fetch git dependencies) and node (to run lifecycle scripts) are required for basic operations.

sentences.en: Acceptance of reduced functionality: yarn relies on external programs for some functionality: in particular git (to fetch git dependencies) and node (to run lifecycle scripts) are required for basic operations.

sentences.zh: 我们还需要支持 Rust 标准库中的目标，以实现 arch 和 os 的组合。

sentences.en: Since it’s modeled after x86 Linux, we can mostly copy from that.
sentences.zh: 由于它是根据 x86 Linux 建模的，因此我们大部分可以从中复制。

sentences.zh: Cargo 和 rustc 的许多选项需要将所有内容联系在一起（不稳定的功能标志、具有 C 依赖项的 sysroot、libc 和 linux-raw-sys 的 Cargo 覆盖，……）；我们为它们提供了包装脚本，因此用户可以使用简单的 Cargo build --target wasm32-browserpod-linux-musl 进行编译。

content_html_zh:
今天，我们发布了 BrowserPod 3.0，完全支持在浏览器中运行任何 Rust 应用程序，对 Node.js 进行了许多修复，并初始支持 Python。

在标准库功能和第三方板条箱兼容性方面，我们的 Rust 支持超出了现有 Wasm 目标通常可以实现的目标。 程序可以访问文件系统、发出网络请求、运行子进程以及与并发运行的应用程序交互。 所有这一切都无需更改任何一行代码！

在下面的演示中，您可以看到 Yarn 6 的预览版本（用 Rust 编写）安装 NPM 项目：

什么是 BrowserPod

BrowserPod 是一个浏览器内代码沙箱。 其目标是通过将应用程序编译为 WebAssembly 并提供完整的 Linux 系统调用接口，使任何 Linux 应用程序都可以在现代浏览器中运行。

它提供高效、本地持久的虚拟文件系统、用于下载包或调用 API 的出站互联网访问，以及用于公开本地开发服务器的入站连接。 BrowserPod 通过在独立的 Worker 上运行每个线程或进程来支持真正的并行性，同时为所有正在运行的程序提供一致的系统视图。 出于所有目的，它可以被视为 Web 平台的操作系统内核，在 WebAssembly 中实现。

这组功能使 BrowserPod 非常适合安全的浏览器内代理代码执行、基于 Web 的 IDE 和开发环境、交互式文档和现场演示、教育平台以及受益于 Web 应用程序内部沙盒执行的其他应用程序。

为什么现在生锈？

BrowserPod 的目标是在浏览器中运行整个 Linux 用户空间。 在大多数情况下，这过去意味着编译一堆 C/C++ 项目。 大多数动态语言（例如 Python、JavaScript 或 Ruby）都在解释器和运行时上运行，而这些解释器和运行时通常也是用 C/C++ 编写的，因此拥有 C/C++ 工具链（在我们的例子中为 Cheerp）会让您走得更远。

如今，这种说法越来越不真实了。 Rust 和 Go 等流行语言像 C/C++ 一样提前编译，并拥有自己的工具链。

许多 Node.js 的构建工具都是用 Rust 编写（或重写）的。 出于这些原因，Rust 始终是我们 BrowserPod 路线图的一部分，但由于我们社区成员在 Discord 上提供的具体用例，我们决定将其优先于 Python 和 Ruby。

Yarn 包管理器的一位维护者表示有兴趣构建一个交互式文档页面，该页面具有真正的 Yarn 构建并在 BrowserPod 上运行。 但与以前的版本（即 JavaScript）相反，即将发布的 Yarn 6 版本是用 Rust 构建的。

这是我们认为 BrowserPod 真正大放异彩的用例之一，因此我们立即开始研究它！ 我们花了一周的时间才得到第一个原型，我们可以立即看到潜力，但还有更多我们预期的活动部件。

“支持”Rust 是什么意思

在以前版本的 BrowserPod 中，我们专注于 Node.js。 我们的用户不必担心 BrowserPod 目标的编译，因为我们自己提供了预编译的 Node.js 构建。

Rust 程序的行为非常不同，因为它们需要使用 rustc 提前编译。 目前的情况是，用户需要离线编译程序并将生成的二进制文件添加到 Pod 中。 有趣的是，rustc 本身是用 Rust 编写的。 原则上，我们可以允许用户直接在浏览器中编译他们的 Rust 程序。 我们需要一些额外的功能来实现这一目标，但这将在不久的将来实现。

今天有效地“支持 Rust”归结为提供一个 Rust 工具链，可以为 BrowserPod 目标生成 Wasm 二进制文件。

现有 Rust WebAssembly 目标

幸运的是，我们可以从坚实的基础开始。 Rust 已经支持多种 Wasm 目标，即：

  • wasm32-unknown-unknown：此目标是最准系统且与平台无关的。 就其本身而言，它不会对其运行环境做出任何假设，但像 wasm-bindgen 和 web-sys 这样的包可以与 JS 和 Web 环境进行通信。 如果您从一开始就有意以 Web 为目标，则此目标是有意义的。 缺少许多标准库功能。
  • wasm32-unknown-emscripten：此目标适用于针对 Web 的独立程序。 它可以直接与 JavaScript 代码交互，并且已经封装了许多 Web API 以方便使用。 它还在一定程度上模拟了一些 POSIX API，但许多 Rust 标准库功能并未实现。 一般来说，支持这个目标需要大量的重写。
  • wasm32-wasip1 / wasm32-wasip2 / wasm32-wasip3：这些是 WASI 目标。 它们原则上可以在任何环境中运行，尽管它们的主要用途是在浏览器之外的 WebAssembly。 因此，它们不假设 JS 的存在，但它们为应用程序提供 I/O 设施，如文件系统和网络。
  • wasm32-wali-linux-musl：该目标旨在通过提供 x86-64 Linux 系统调用接口作为导入，在 Wasm 运行时中运行现有的 Linux 应用程序。 它的主要用例是在浏览器之外，目前主要是一个学术项目。

为什么不直接选择WASI呢？

我们最初的计划是在 BrowserPod 之上实现 WASI（WebAssembly 系统接口）层。 该解决方案将使任何针对 WASI 的程序立即与 BrowserPod 兼容，无论它是用 Rust、Go、C 还是其他语言编写的。

但当尝试将现有 Rust 程序编译为 WASI 时，我们很快意识到这不仅仅是切换构建目标的问题。

以纱线为例。 为 WASI 编译它需要：

  • 使用 std::os::wasi 替换 std::os::unix 的特定于平台的代码：这是可行的，尽管映射不是 1:1（例如 WASI 中没有绝对符号链接）。
  • 删除线程使用：wasm32-wasip3 有一些有限的协作线程支持（没有真正的并行性），但它非常新，并且标准库和 tokio 都不支持。
  • 接受减少的功能：yarn 依赖外部程序来实现某些功能：特别是基本操作需要 git（用于获取 git 依赖项）和 Node（用于运行生命周期脚本）。

BrowserPod 已经解决了这些问题，因此我们决定跳过中间人并实现我们自己的 Rust 目标：wasm32-browserpod-linux-musl。

制定我们自己的 Rust 目标

定义自定义 Rust 目标非常简单：您可以在 .json 文件中定义目标的属性：

然后将此文件的路径作为 --target 参数传递。

需要一些不稳定的功能，因此我们必须使用夜间版本的编译器。 我们还需要支持 Rust 标准库中的目标，以实现 arch 和 os 的组合。 由于它是根据 x86 Linux 建模的，因此我们大部分可以从中复制。 最后，我们需要重写几个基础库：libc（我们需要链接到我们自己的 musl libc 构建）和 linux-raw-sys（我们只需选择 libc 后备）。

Cargo 和 rustc 的许多选项需要将所有内容联系在一起（不稳定的功能标志、具有 C 依赖项的 sysroot、libc 和 linux-raw-sys 的 Cargo 覆盖，……）；我们为它们提供了包装脚本，因此用户可以使用简单的 Cargo build --target wasm32-browserpod-linux-musl 进行编译。

我们一路上所做的黑客

在理想的世界中，这就是我们所需要的。 不幸的是，我们需要处理第三方依赖的混乱现实。

如前所述，Rust 已经支持多个 Wasm 目标。 许多库可以针对其中一个或多个目标进行编译，但通常会减少功能，或者假设 arch="wasm32" 意味着“在浏览器的主线程中运行”，以及其他任意约束。

为了实现在不更改代码的情况下编译项目的目标，我们需要避免所有条件编译，这些条件编译会错误地将我们的目标归类为“减少功能”的目标。

如果您仔细查看上面目标定义的 json 片段，您会注意到两个有趣的事情：

  • target_family: ["unix"]：最初，我们有 ["unix"、"wasm"]，但许多板条箱使用 wasm 目标系列来表示“独立 Web 构建”、“WASI”、“无文件系统”或类似含义。 删除“wasm”似乎完全无害。
  • arch: "wasm64"：这更令人惊讶，但不幸的是也是必要的。 arch="wasm32" 通常用于检测独立的 Web 目标（例如，reqwest 将使用 fetch() 实现替换整个 HTTP 客户端）。 您可能会认为某些东西会因此而中断，但像指针大小这样的重要信息是单独定义的，并且传递到 LLVM 后端的实际目标仍然是 wasm32，所以一切顺利！

当然，我们很想摆脱这些黑客行为，但正确的解决方案需要生态系统意识到功能齐全的 Wasm 目标的存在，这需要时间（但我们有一个计划）。

未来计划

我解释了为什么现有的 Wasm 目标不适合我们，但我掩盖了 wasm32-wali-linux-musl。

尽管针对的是本机 Wasm 运行时而不是浏览器，但 WALI（WebAssembly Linux Interface）与 BrowserPod 具有相同的核心目标：将未经修改的 Linux 应用程序编译为 Wasm。 主要区别在于，BrowserPod 针对的是 x86 版本的 Linux 系统调用，而 WALI 则针对的是 x86-64 版本。 选择 BrowserPod 是因为它的系统调用实现与 CheerpX 共享，CheerpX 是 x86 Linux 二进制文件的虚拟机（您可能从 WebVM 中知道它）。

CheerpX 正在努力支持 x86-64 二进制文件，因此将来我们可以简单地采用 WALI 作为我们的目标（对于 Rust 和 C/C++）。

这将有很多好处：

  • 它已经是受支持的 Rust 目标
  • 我们可以在浏览器内部和外部运行相同的 Wasm 二进制文件
  • 我们可以联手解决上游第三方库的问题

我们对这个方向感到非常兴奋，并将在未来对此进行更多讨论！
